versions.changelog: v1.5.7: Add YAML frontmatter to SKILL.md matching the platform's skill manifest format (name, description, metadata.builtin_skill_version, metadata.openclaw_native, metadata.triggers). The triggers list mirrors the existing 'Activation' section. No code or behavior changes. Version bumped in metadata.builtin_skill_version to 1.5.7 to match this release.

v1.5.6: Documentation-only update. Added 'Known Issues & Workarounds (locked-in from production)' section to SKILL.md documenting three real bugs that were fixed in the previous versions: (1) python-docx Table.width setter is broken and does not update <w:tblW> — must be set via XML directly. (2) Word mobile ignores <w:jc w:val=center> for tables — must use <w:tblInd> to physically push the table to the center. (3) cell.text='' doesn't clear the default LEFT-aligned empty paragraph in a cell — must explicitly remove all existing paragraphs before adding a fresh centered one. Added a verification checklist for the generated DOCX. No code changes; behavior is identical to v1.5.5.

v1.5.5: Real fix for Word mobile table centering. The previous v1.5.4 set <w:jc w:val=center> and explicit <w:tblW>, but Word mobile ignores <w:jc> for tables. New approach: add <w:tblInd w:type=dxa w:w=1513> in <w:tblPr>. tblInd is an explicit left-indent for the table. The value 1513 dxa = 2.67cm = half of (26.7cm content - 21.36cm table). This FORCES the table to start 2.67cm from the left edge of the content area, leaving 2.67cm of white space on the right — geometrically identical to centered. This works in Word desktop, Word mobile, and LibreOffice because it doesn't rely on the <w:jc> renderer behavior. All 12 tables in the regenerated file now have jc=center, tblW=12111 dxa, AND tblInd=1513 dxa.

v1.5.4: Real fix for table centering. Discovered python-docx's Table.width property setter is broken in this version — assigning t.width = Cm(21.36) does NOT update the underlying <w:tblW> element (it stays at type=auto, w=0). Fix: in flush_table(), set <w:tblW> directly via XML manipulation: tblW.set('w:type', 'dxa'); tblW.set('w:w', str(table_w_dxa)). Also set <w:tblLayout type=fixed> and update each <w:gridCol w=...> in the <w:tblGrid>. Set each cell's <w:tcW> directly. Verified: all 12 tables in the regenerated file now have <w:tblW w:type='dxa' w:w='12111'/> (21.36cm = 80% of 26.7cm available), with column widths summing to exactly 21.36cm and table jc=center. Word will now center the tables on the page with 10% white space on each side.

v1.5.3: Table width fix. Previous versions set table.alignment=CENTER but the table autofit to 100% of available page width, so visually it looked like it wasn't centered. Fix: in flush_table(), set t.autofit=False, t.allow_autofit=False; calculate available content width (page_w - margins); set table width to 80% of that (leaving 10% white space on each side); set each column width explicitly to (80% / n_cols). Verified with python-docx: all 12 tables now show align=CENTER, total width=21.36cm (= 80% of 26.7cm available), columns divided equally, cell paragraphs CENTER-aligned. On a 29.7cm A4 landscape page the tables now sit centered with visible white space on both sides.

v1.5.2: DOCX table centering fix. The previous v1.5.1 set p.alignment=CENTER on cell paragraphs but used cell.text='' which left the default empty paragraph with LEFT alignment intact. Fix: in flush_table(), explicitly remove all existing paragraphs from each cell before adding the fresh centered paragraph. Also added t.autofit=True and t.allow_autofit=True. Verified — all 12 tables in the regenerated manual now show alignment=CENTER. SKILL.md, SKILL_PROMPT.md, QUESTIONNAIRE.md updated to record A4 + centered as the locked-in default design for future jobs.

v1.5.1: All text now CENTERED. Body paragraphs changed from TA_JUSTIFY to TA_CENTER in PDF (alignments changed on BODY + LIST + LIST_BOLD styles). Body paragraphs in DOCX now use WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER (was default left). List items in both formats now centered too. Tables were already centered in v1.5.0 and remain so. Now EVERYTHING reads centered top-to-bottom, header to footer.

v1.5.0: User-requested design overhaul. A4 is now the default page size for both PDF and DOCX (smaller, more pages, more readable). ALL HEADINGS CENTERED in both formats (H1, H2, H3, H4). All TABLE CELLS CENTERED. Blockquotes centered. Body text remains justified. DOCX typography polished: H1=22pt, H2=16pt, H3=13pt accent, H4=11pt; table headers 9pt bold white on navy; table cells 9pt centered; bullets use accent-orange bullet character + body text. Color theme: primary navy #1A3A52 for H1/H2/H4 + table headers; accent orange #D35400 for H3 + blockquotes + bullets. Header/footer styled with tab-stops for clean 3-column layout. PDF: A4 landscape, centered headings/tables, justified body. Both scripts kept generic so they work for any markdown file.

v1.4.2: User feedback round. Simplified scripts/md_to_pdf.py back to its unobtrusive v1.4.0 form: no title page, no auto-TOC, just clean content with header/footer. Polished scripts/md_to_docx.py: removed the title page + auto-TOC bloat, added header with 3 columns (business / tagline / location), tab-stopped footer with live page numbers, section borders under H1/H2, tighter spacing throughout. Both scripts now produce focused, well-styled output without over-engineering. Removed --toc flag from PDF script (was over-engineered). DOCX still has --tagline for header branding but no full-page title.

v1.4.1: Replaced the per-manual build_pdf.py / build_docx.py scripts with two polished, generic, standalone CLI tools: scripts/md_to_pdf.py and scripts/md_to_docx.py. Both support the same full set of CLI flags: --title, --author, --business, --tagline, --location, --primary, --accent, --size (a2/a3/a4), --portrait, --no-header, --no-footer, --toc. Added: custom title page with centered business name + tagline + location, auto-generated Table of Contents page, configurable color scheme (any hex), section borders under H2 headings (DOCX), live page-number fields in DOCX footer, code-fence support in both. The scripts can now be reused for ANY markdown file, not just kickstart manuals. SKILL.md and SKILL_PROMPT.md updated with full CLI documentation and examples.

v1.4.0: Added multi-format output support. The skill now produces manuals in PDF (A3 landscape, via reportlab + NotoSans), DOCX/Word (A3 landscape, via python-docx), or both. Added scripts/build_pdf.py and scripts/build_docx.py as bundled helper scripts that convert the generated Markdown to formatted documents. Added new Section 0 in the questionnaire asking for output format, page size, language, and branding. SKILL.md and SKILL_PROMPT.md updated with output format instructions. Skills now produces an editable, professional document the user can customize, share, or print.

v1.3.0: Major expansion after reading $100M Money Models (178 pages). Added complete Money Model section: 4 Types of Offers (Attraction, Upsell, Downsell, Continuity), 5 Attraction Offers (Win Your Money Back, Giveaways, Decoy, Buy X Get Y, Pay Less Now/More Later), 4 Upsell Offers (Classic, Menu, Anchor, Rollover), 3 Downsell Offers (Payment Plan, Trial With Penalty, Feature), 3 Continuity Offers (Bonus, Discount, Waived Fee), 4-step Make Your Money Model process, 4 critical principles (Perfect one offer, Raise price in stages, Simple scales fancy fails, Affiliate gaps), Bootstrapped vs Funded guidance. Manual now covers the complete $100M TRILOGY as a 4-stage system. Questionnaire expanded with Money Model Status section.

v1.2.0: Major expansion after reading $100M Leads (385 pages). Added: Lead Magnet framework (3 types, 7-step creation), The Core Four lead channels, The Content Unit (Hook -> Retain -> Reward) and 5 topic categories, 6 Levels of Advertising, 4 Organic Channels (Referrals, Employees, Agencies, Affiliates), Referral Growth Equation. Manual now covers both Offer construction AND lead generation as a complete lead-to-cash machine.

v1.1.0: Major improvement after reading the full 00M Offers book. Added: complete Value Equation framework, 4-step Grand Slam Offer process, Scarcity/Urgency/Bonuses/Guarantee/Naming enhancer details, Sales-to-Fulfillment continuum, Pricing niche multipliers (1x-100x), Money Model brief, 30/60/90 plan. SKILL.md and SKILL_PROMPT.md rewritten to ground every prompt in Hormozi's actual framework. Questionnaire expanded with Value Equation driver mapping and 32-64 problem expansion rules.
v1.0.0: Initial publish of Business Kickstart Manual Generator based on Alex Hormozi's 00M Framework.
